title: Natural Domain and Range of a Radical with a Quadratic Radicand
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Natural Domain and Range
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine the natural domain and range of the real-valued function g(x) = sqrt(x^2 - 3x).

steps.title: Formulate the Non-Negativity Condition
steps.explanation: Because the expression is governed by a square root, the quadratic radicand x^2 - 3x must be non-negative.
steps.why: Even-degree roots require non-negative radicands to evaluate to real numbers.

steps.title: Factor the Quadratic Radicand
steps.explanation: Factor out x to identify the roots of x(x - 3) = 0, which occur at x = 0 and x = 3.
steps.why: Factoring locates the critical boundary points where a continuous polynomial can change sign.

steps.title: Perform Sign Analysis Across Test Intervals
steps.explanation: For x < 0, both x and x - 3 are negative, so their product is positive. For 0 < x < 3, x is positive and x - 3 is negative, so their product is negative. For x > 3, both factors are positive, so their product is positive. Including the roots 0 and 3 gives (-inf, 0] U [3, inf).
steps.why: The product of two real factors is non-negative if and only if both factors have the same sign or at least one is zero.

steps.title: Determine the Output Range
steps.explanation: At the boundary points x = 0 and x = 3, g(0) = g(3) = 0. As x approaches positive or negative infinity, x^2 - 3x grows without bound, so sqrt(x^2 - 3x) attains all values in [0, inf).
steps.why: The principal square root is continuous and maps the unbounded non-negative radicand onto [0, inf).
